points.name: Hegu
points.place: On the mound between thumb and index
points.for: Headache; pain of the face and teeth.
points.caution: Not in pregnancy.

points.name: Neiguan
points.place: Three fingers above the wrist crease
points.for: Nausea; palpitations; poor sleep.

points.name: Zusanli
points.place: Four fingers below the kneecap
points.for: Digestion, tiredness, heavy legs.

points.name: Fengchi
points.place: Below the skull, between the neck cords
points.for: Headache; dizziness; a stiff, sore neck.

points.name: Sanyinjiao
points.place: Four fingers above the inner ankle
points.for: Period pain, irregular periods, poor sleep.
points.caution: Never in pregnancy; if you may be pregnant, ask a practitioner first.

points.name: Taichong
points.place: Top of foot, where the toe bones meet
points.for: Headache; dizziness; painful periods.
points.caution: In pregnancy, ask a practitioner first.

points.name: Baihui
points.place: Top of the head, between the ear tips
points.for: Headache and dizziness, poor sleep, a poor memory.

points.name: Danzhong
points.place: Breastbone, at the fourth rib space
points.for: Chest tightness, palpitations, cough.

points.name: Shenmen
points.place: On the wrist crease, little-finger end
points.for: Poor sleep, a restless mind, forgetfulness.

points.name: Lieque
points.place: In the groove above the wrist bone
points.for: Cough, headache, a stiff neck.

points.name: Taixi
points.place: Between inner ankle and Achilles tendon
points.for: Ringing ears; low-back ache; poor sleep.

points.name: Weizhong
points.place: Centre of the crease behind the knee
points.for: Low back and spine ache; weak legs.
points.caution: Skip over swollen, tender or varicose veins behind the knee.

points.name: Chengshan
points.place: Hollow below the calf muscle
points.for: Calf cramps; haemorrhoids; constipation.
points.caution: Skip a calf that is suddenly swollen, hot or sore, and see a doctor.

points.name: Houxi
points.place: Behind the little-finger knuckle
points.for: Stiff, aching neck and head; low back pain.

points.name: Waiguan
points.place: Three fingers above the back wrist
points.for: Headache; ringing ears; aching arm.

points.name: Neiting
points.place: At the web of the second and third toes
points.for: Toothache, sore throat, nosebleed.

points.name: Yinlingquan
points.place: Below the knob at the top of the shin
points.for: Bloating, swelling from fluid, knee pain.

points.name: Quchi
points.place: Outer elbow, past the end of the crease
points.for: An aching arm, fever, itchy skin.

points.name: Dazhui
points.place: Below the big bump at the neck’s base
points.for: Colds and fever, a stiff neck, shoulder and back ache.

points.name: Zhongfu

points.for: Cough, wheezing, a full, tight chest.

points.name: Yunmen

points.for: Cough, wheezing, an aching chest and shoulder.

points.name: Tianfu

points.for: Cough, nosebleed, an aching upper arm.

points.name: Xiabai

points.for: Cough, dry retching, an aching upper arm.

points.name: Chize

points.for: Cough, sore throat, an aching elbow.

points.name: Kongzui

points.name: Taiyuan

points.name: Yuji

points.name: Yangxi

points.name: Pianli

points.name: Wenliu

points.name: Shanglian

points.name: Shousanli

points.name: Zhouliao

points.name: Shouwuli

points.name: Binao

points.for: Shoulder and arm ache, a stiff neck, headache.

points.for: Sore throat, sudden hoarseness, cough.

points.name: Yingxiang

points.name: Chengqi

points.name: Sibai
points.place: Below the pupil, on the cheekbone dip
points.for: Red, itchy eyes, twitching eyelids, face pain.
points.caution: Close to the eye: press on bone only, never on the eye.

points.name: Juliao
points.place: Below the pupil, level with the nostril
points.for: Toothache, nosebleed, a puffy cheek.

points.name: Dicang
points.place: Just out from the corner of the mouth
points.for: Drooling, a drooping mouth corner, toothache.

points.name: Daying
points.place: In front of the jaw angle, at a pulse
points.for: Toothache, a puffy cheek, a stiff jaw.
points.caution: A facial pulse beats here; keep the touch light.

points.name: Jiache
points.place: On the jaw muscle above the jaw angle
points.for: Toothache, a stiff jaw, a puffy cheek.

points.name: Xiaguan
points.place: In front of the ear, under the cheekbone
points.for: Jaw pain, toothache, ringing ears.

points.name: Touwei
points.place: At the corner of the forehead hairline
points.for: Headache, dizziness, sore eyes.

points.name: Renying
points.place: Side of the neck, at the neck pulse
points.for: Sore throat, a swollen neck, a tight chest.
points.caution: Over the carotid artery; keep pressure off the neck pulse.

points.name: Shuitu
points.place: Lower neck, at the front muscle edge
points.for: Sore throat, cough, shortness of breath.
points.caution: Keep off the pulse and the windpipe; never both sides at once.

points.name: Qishe
points.place: Above the inner end of the collarbone
points.for: Sore throat, hiccups, a stiff neck.
points.caution: Keep off any pulse; never press both sides at once.

points.name: Quepen
points.place: In the hollow above the collarbone
points.for: Cough, shortness of breath, sore throat.
points.caution: The top of the lung and large vessels lie beneath; keep it light.

points.name: Qihu
points.place: Just below the middle of the collarbone
points.for: Cough, wheezing, hiccups.

points.name: Kufang
points.place: First rib gap, in line with the nipple
points.for: Cough, shortness of breath, a full, sore chest.

points.name: Wuyi
points.place: Second rib gap, in line with the nipple
points.for: Cough, a full, aching chest.

points.name: Yingchuang
points.place: Third rib gap, in line with the nipple
points.for: Cough, shortness of breath, aching chest and ribs.

points.name: Ruzhong
points.place: At the centre of the nipple
points.for: A landmark for finding the chest points around it.
points.caution: Classical texts warn against working on this point.

points.name: Rugen
points.place: Below the nipple, at the breast root
points.for: Low milk supply, cough, chest pain.
points.caution: Not over a breast lump, redness or warmth; have a doctor check it.

points.name: Taiyi

points.for: Stomach ache, vomiting.
points.caution: Not on the belly in pregnancy.

points.caution: Not on the belly in pregnancy.

points.name: Guilai

points.caution: Not on the belly in pregnancy.

points.name: Shangjuxu

points.name: Lougu

points.name: Diji

points.name: Daheng

points.caution: Not on the belly in pregnancy.

points.name: Fu’ai

points.caution: Fainting or collapse needs emergency help; call for it first.

points.name: Duiduan
points.place: Centre of the upper lip’s edge
points.for: Sore, swollen gums; a blocked nose.

points.name: Yinjiao
points.place: Inside the upper lip, at the gum
points.for: Sore, swollen gums; bad breath.

points.name: Huiyin
points.place: Between the anus and the genitals
points.for: Difficult urination, haemorrhoids, genital itching.
points.caution: Intimate area; do not press it yourself.

points.name: Qugu
points.place: On the top edge of the pubic bone
points.for: Difficult urination, period pain, irregular periods.
points.caution: Not in pregnancy.

points.name: Zhongji
points.place: A thumb-width above the pubic bone
points.for: Period pain, irregular periods, bladder discomfort.
points.caution: Not in pregnancy.

points.name: Guanyuan
points.place: Four finger-widths below the navel
points.for: Period pain, frequent urination, tiredness with a feeling of cold.
points.caution: Not in pregnancy.

points.name: Shimen
points.place: Two thumb-widths below the navel
points.for: Belly pain, loose stools, difficult urination.
points.caution: Not in pregnancy.

points.name: Qihai
points.place: Two finger-widths below the navel
points.for: Belly pain, constipation or loose stools, low energy.
points.caution: Not in pregnancy.

points.name: Yinjiao
points.place: One thumb-width below the navel
points.for: Belly pain, loose stools, irregular periods.
points.caution: Not in pregnancy.

points.name: Shenque
points.place: The centre of the navel
points.for: Belly pain, loose stools.
points.caution: Never press into the navel: the skin is thin and the bowel lies just beneath.

points.name: Shuifen
points.place: One thumb-width above the navel
points.for: Belly pain, loose stools, puffy swelling.

points.name: Xiawan
points.place: Two thumb-widths above the navel
points.for: Bloating, indigestion, hiccups.

points.name: Jianli
points.place: Four finger-widths above the navel
points.for: Stomach ache, bloating, poor appetite.

points.name: Zhongwan
points.place: Midway from navel to breastbone tip
points.for: Stomach ache, bloating, acid reflux.

points.name: Shangwan
points.place: A thumb-width above Zhongwan
points.for: Stomach ache, retching and vomiting, poor appetite.

points.name: Juque
points.place: Two thumb-widths below the breastbone
points.for: Palpitations, bloating, vomiting.

points.name: Jiuwei
points.place: A thumb-width below the breastbone tip
points.for: Chest tightness, palpitations, hiccups.

points.name: Zhongting
points.place: Lower end of the breastbone
points.for: Fullness of the chest and ribs, trouble swallowing, vomiting.

points.name: Yutang
points.place: Breastbone, at the third rib space
points.for: Chest tightness, cough, sore throat.

points.name: Zigong
points.place: Breastbone, at the second rib space
points.for: Chest tightness, cough, shortness of breath.

points.name: Huagai
points.place: Breastbone, at the first rib space
points.for: Cough, wheezing, chest and rib pain.

points.name: Xuanji
points.place: Just below the notch atop the breastbone
points.for: Cough, sore throat, a full chest.

points.name: Tiantu
points.place: In the notch at the base of the throat
points.for: Cough, a lump-in-the-throat feeling, a hoarse voice.
points.caution: Never press hard or back into the throat: the windpipe lies just beneath.

points.name: Lianquan
points.place: Under the chin, above the Adam’s apple
points.for: Mouth and tongue sores, drooling, trouble swallowing.
points.caution: Never press hard on the throat.

points.name: Chengjiang
points.place: Centre of the crease below the lower lip
points.for: Swollen gums, drooling, mouth sores.

conditions.name: Tension headache
conditions.summary: Tension headache is a dull, band-like pain across the forehead or base of the skull; classical acupressure points include LI4, GB20, and LV3.

conditions.name: Anxiety
conditions.summary: For mild anxiety, classical acupressure reaches for points like HT7, PC6, and Yintang — typically alongside slow breathing.

conditions.name: Travel nausea
conditions.summary: PC6 (Neiguan) on the inner forearm is the classical acupoint for travel and morning nausea and the point behind motion-sickness wristbands.

conditions.name: Insomnia
conditions.summary: For sleep, classical acupressure pairs a calming point at the wrist, HT7, with a grounding point on the sole, KI1.

conditions.name: Period pain
conditions.summary: For period pain, TCM most often draws on SP6, LV3, and local abdominal points — though some (like SP6) are avoided during pregnancy.

conditions.name: Back pain
conditions.summary: Classical acupressure for lower back pain often combines BL23, BL40, and GB30, chosen by where the pain is located.

conditions.name: Neck and shoulder strain from desk work
conditions.summary: Neck and shoulder strain from desk work eases first with breaks every hour or two, forearm support and neck exercise; classical acupressure adds GB20, GB21 and LI11 as an optional comfort pause, on limited evidence.

conditions.name: Nausea after surgery or chemotherapy
conditions.summary: For nausea after surgery or chemotherapy, classical acupressure reaches first for PC6 (Neiguan) on the inner wrist, with LI4 and ST36 as companions — always as an add-on to prescribed anti-sickness medicine, never a replacement.

conditions.name: Bloating
conditions.summary: For a bloated, distended belly, Chinese nursing care pairs clockwise belly massage with CV12, ST25 and CV6 on the abdomen and ST36 and PC6 on the leg and wrist; skip CV6 in pregnancy.

conditions.name: Constipation
conditions.summary: For ordinary constipation, habits come first; classical acupressure adds a clockwise belly massage and the points ST25, TH6, ST36, and ST37.

conditions.name: Knee arthritis pain
conditions.summary: For knee osteoarthritis pain, exercise and weight management come first; classical acupressure adds six points ringing the knee: SP10, ST34, ST35, SP9, GB34 and ST36.

conditions.name: After a stroke
conditions.summary: After a stroke, a national Chinese nursing protocol names GB21, LI11, TH5 and LI4 on the arm and GB34, BL40 and GB39 on the leg; a carer presses them lightly on the weak side, alongside rehabilitation, never on spastic muscle or a swollen limb.

conditions.name: Fatigue
conditions.summary: For everyday tiredness of the depleted kind, Chinese medicine reaches for ST36 (Zusanli), SP6, CV6 and CV4 below the navel, and LI4; research on hand-pressed points comes mainly from fatigue after cancer treatment and in haemodialysis.

conditions.name: Labour pain
conditions.summary: Sanyinjiao (SP6) and hegu (LI4), pressed by a birth partner through contractions, only once labour has started at 37 weeks or later and only with the midwife's or obstetric team's agreement; never to start labour or before term.
